newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong stocks slip in later trade, close lower.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks slip in later trade, close lower.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks lost momentum in late afternoon trade to close marginally down on Monday, chiefly due to weakness in properties and conglomerates as well as banking giant HSBC Holdings, brokers said.
"Today we saw a couple of the big cap stocks doing well, but that only (temporarily) masked other weaknesses," said Glenn Lesko, equities trader at ABN Amro Hoare Govett Asia.

The Hang Seng Index slipped 34.10 points or 0.22 percent to close at 15,536.30 after dipping to a low of 15,370.42 in early morning trade. Turnover was a robust HK$17.64 billion, though down from Friday's HK$20.82 billion.
Fewer issues were still showing the market's recent upward momentum, said Lesko. "Unless properties and conglomerates start participating, people are going to get nervous," he said.

The index fell sharply just after the open, shaken by Wall Street's Friday slump, when the Dow Industrials closed down 130.31 points at 7,890.46. It was a weak finish to a record-setting week when the Dow and the Hang Seng both set new highs.
Hongkong Telecom and Hang Seng Bank held the index up for a good part of the day, said Lesko.

Hongkong Telecom inched up HK$0.10 to HK$20.25. Hang Seng Bank put on HK$4.00 to close at HK$115.00, after touching an all-time high of HK$117.00. The bank and its parent HSBC Holdings will report interim earnings on August 4.
HSBC, which has led the market for most of 1997, was the most actively traded issue. The share closed HK$3.00 lower at HK$262.00 on very heavy trade of HK$1.55 billion.
Bank of East Asia rose an all-time high of HK$33.10, then eased back to close HK$0.90 up at HK$32.90.
Properties were the worst performing sector, led down by New World Development.
The property developer and China investor lost HK$0.90 to close at HK$47.40 on low turnover of HK$101.36 million. Sun Hung Kai Properties lost HK$0.50 to close at HK$88.50.
"Most property counters are still under pressure and we can't sustain the rally without properties," said Steve Cheng, sales director at Lippo Securities.
Among the conglomerates CITIC Pacific fell the hardest, losing HK$0.60 to HK$46.40.
The Hang Seng China Enterprise Index of H shares also lost 13.60 points or 1.19 percent to 1,133.41. Beiren Printing led, falling HK$0.27 or 11.25 percent to HK$2.40.
